claims.head: Power against power
claims.call: The Flyers’ L1 (Dvorak, Zegras and Foerster) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Avalanche’s first line.
claims.body: At home, the Flyers keep sending Zegras’s line (Dvorak, Zegras and Foerster) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Tocchet has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Avalanche’s first line is Lehkonen, MacKinnon and Nečas.

claims.gist: At home, Rick Tocchet likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Avalanche’s first line.

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 4 of their last 8 games, including the last one. Nazem Kadri takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L4. Noah Juulsen is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Manson and Malinski.
T.J. Hughes is day to day, reported after he played in their last game.
Gavin Brindley was added to the roster on Oct 15 and has played beside Parker Kelly and Fedor Svechkov.
Zachary L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 20% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Sean Couturier is day to day, reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Owen Tippett is on injured reserve and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Tyson Foerster is day to day, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Cam York is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Nick Seeler has taken his spot beside Jamie Drysdale.
Oliver Bonk was added to the roster on Oct 12 and has played beside Travis Sanheim.
Jack Studnicka was added to the roster on Oct 14 and has played beside Michael Bunting and Noel Acciari.
David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 44% of the team’s power-play time in 8 games, up from 2% last season.

PHI.head: The Flyers have a hill to climb
PHI.body: Even though Philadelphia has home-ice advantage, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, and the Flyers will be without Tippett. The Flyers’ best way through is a penalty kill that holds up.

COL.head: The Avalanche have a lot going for them
COL.body: Even though Philadelphia has home-ice advantage, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, and the Flyers will be without Tippett. The Flyers’ way back in is a penalty kill that holds up.

story.head: Juulsen returns to Philadelphia

items.text: Noah Juulsen faces Philadelphia for the first time since leaving.
The Avalanche are newly without T.J. Hughes.
Nathan MacKinnon has a point in six straight games against Philadelphia, and 10 points in his last six against them.
The Flyers are newly without Sean Couturier, Owen Tippett and Tyson Foerster, and have been without Cam York since Oct 8.
